context:
542:
  • Ferrum Edge runs as a native binary on the host — zero container overhead.

543:
  • Kong runs {"natively on the host (installed via package manager) — no container overhead." if meta.get("kong_native") else "inside a Docker container. On macOS, Docker Desktop runs containers in a Linux VM with userspace networking, which adds ~0.1–0.5 ms per round-trip (port-mapped) plus higher CPU scheduling variance (~9.5x). On Linux with --network host, Docker overhead is negligible (<5 µs). To eliminate this overhead on Linux, install Kong natively via the official apt/yum packages."}

544:
  • Tyk runs inside a Docker container (no official macOS binary; Linux-only native packages available via packagecloud). The same Docker overhead caveats as Kong apply. Additionally, Tyk requires Redis which also runs in a container.

545:
  • KrakenD runs inside a Docker container (Go-based, stateless gateway). The same Docker overhead caveats apply. KrakenD is configured with no-op encoding for raw response pass-through, matching the minimal-overhead proxy behavior of other gateways. Key-auth benchmarks are excluded because API key authentication requires KrakenD Enterprise Edition.

546:
  • Envoy Proxy runs inside a Docker container (C++-based, high-performance proxy). The same Docker overhead caveats apply. Envoy is configured as a minimal HTTP reverse proxy with static route configuration, no access logging, and connection pooling defaults. Key-auth benchmarks are excluded as Envoy’s ext_authz filter requires an external authorization service.

547:
  • HTTPS tests measure TLS termination at the gateway (client → HTTPS → gateway → HTTP → backend). E2E TLS tests measure full encryption (client → HTTPS → gateway → HTTPS → backend), the most secure pattern.

548:
  • All gateways run sequentially (one at a time) to avoid resource contention on the host.

549:
  • The /api/echo endpoint receives a POST with a ~10 KB JSON payload that the backend echoes back, measuring realistic request+response body proxying overhead.

550:
  • Each test includes a {meta.get("duration", "30s")} measured run preceded by a warm-up phase (results discarded).

551:
  • To get the fairest comparison on macOS, install Kong natively and run the benchmark again. Tyk results on macOS should be interpreted with Docker overhead in mind (~0.1–0.5 ms added latency, ~5-15% throughput reduction).
